title: Game Math Part 2 · Rendering 5: Building Meshes and Normals

scenes.title: 정점과 법선으로 표면을 저장하기
lines: What vertex information represents3D shape and lighting directions?
Inspect game roofs and rocks, then calculate indexed connections and memory size.
Compare face and vertex normals and follow the complete neighboring-face accumulation algorithm.
Finally handle sharp edges and triangulation bias and verify the answers on an explicitly defined mesh.

scenes.title: 지붕 패널의 선이 전부 삼각형일까요?
lines: Traverse a roof in Sunset Overdrive. Separate its sloped outline from repeated lines across the surface.
Moving sideways reveals roof and wall faces. It is easy to confuse the surface shape with its pattern.
The next roof has panels and vents. Distinguish shape that changes the outline from lines inside a face.
Rendered pixels cannot prove that each line is a geometric edge: geometry and textures can both create lines.
We therefore define our own small mesh to explain storage, without guessing this game hidden vertex count.

scenes.title: 부피를 만드는 방법과 표면을 저장하는 방법
lines: Shapes have multiple representations. CSG combines solids using union, intersection and difference.
Subtracting a cylinder from a box makes an opening in our solid diagram; it does not identify a game implementation.
Metaballs and implicit functions offer other volume descriptions; representation and display-surface storage serve different purposes.
Triangle meshes connect planar surface pieces; they may represent open cloth or leaves rather than closed solids.
Editing polygons can have varying vertex counts. Rendering triangulates them with the valid methods developed earlier.
We now focus on shared vertices rather than one triangle, translating vertex, edge and face relationships into data.

scenes.title: 네 정점과 두 삼각형의 메모리를 계산하기
lines: Split a quad into triangles012 and023 using four vertices numbered0 through3.
A triangle array stores three records per face, duplicating vertices0 and2 with their attributes.
Indexed storage separates vertex records from integers, with three indices referencing the data for each triangle.
Assume32-byte vertices and2-byte indices. The triangle array uses6 times32, or192 bytes.
Indexed storage uses4 times32 plus6 times2:128 plus12 equals140 bytes.
The source separate local example shares one vertex among six faces:32 plus12 equals44 bytes, unlike the whole quad140.
Total savings depend on attributes, sharing and index format; records may include normals, UVs, colors and skinning data.

scenes.title: 같은 좌표와 같은 정점은 다릅니다
lines: An identical index shares a record; equal positions with different normals or UVs require separate records.
Declare the winding convention. The source clockwise choice must agree with the renderer front-face configuration.
Cyclic012 to120 preserves orientation; swapping two indices to021 reverses it.
The triangles share edge0–2, but a plain index list does not explicitly store neighboring face references.
Editors can store explicit edges and adjacent-face references, as in winged-edge structures.
Boundary edges may have one face and nonmanifold edges more than two, so exactly-two adjacency is not universal.
Triangles can be batched by compatible attributes or materials; editor structures need not match GPU delivery structures.

scenes.title: 벽의 격자를 정점 연결선으로 읽어도 될까요?
lines: Explore the green room in Big Walk, separating the black grid on a nearby panel from curved walls and rocks.
Moving views show panel boundaries and internal lines, separating visible shape from surface detail.
Circular openings and cylindrical bases appear behind them, placing straight patterns and curved outlines together.
Black lines do not prove triangle-index edges; they could be patterns, separate surfaces or another representation.
Our explicit index list proves the0–2 connection; these rendered game pixels do not expose such a list.
Separate shape data from shading directions. The next diagram keeps geometry fixed while changing normals.
Observe the panel faces and outline during the camera movement, motivating face and vertex normals.

scenes.title: 각진 바위와 매끄러운 밝기는 같은 정보일까요?
lines: Move among rocks and cacti in Megabonk. Separate angular rock outlines from brightness inside their faces.
The moving view retains planar rock faces and angular edges; an angular appearance does not expose their normal treatment.
Pass a large rock, then cacti and lower rocks; differently oriented surfaces can receive the same directional light differently.
Materials and shadows also affect brightness. Our next diagram changes only normal direction rather than inferring its numerical values from pixels.
The final interval shows pillars and angular roof forms. Treat geometry positions and lighting directions as separate inputs.
Can shading look smoother without moving vertices? Compare face and vertex normals on our original hexagonal prism.

scenes.title: 면의 법선과 정점의 법선
lines: A face normal is perpendicular to its plane: cross two edges, choose the declared orientation and normalize.
Several planes meet at a vertex, so a sharp corner has no unique geometric surface normal.
For a smooth surface approximated by triangles, vertex normals approximate its directions for shading.
A hexagonal prism can have smoother shading with radial vertex normals while its positions and connections remain unchanged.
Dotting unit normal and unit light direction gives a cosine; renormalization prevents vector length contaminating that angle.
Front-face configuration differs from shading normals; distinguish winding/culling issues from lighting-direction issues.

scenes.title: 밝기를 보간할까, 법선을 보간할까?
lines: Flat shading evaluates a face direction, allowing brightness discontinuities across neighboring faces.
Gouraud shading evaluates lighting at vertices and interpolates the resulting values rather than normals.
Per-pixel shading interpolates vertex normals, renormalizes them and evaluates lighting at covered samples.
A half blend of right and up gives(.5,.5), whose length is about.707 rather than one.
Normalizing produces components about.707; do this before using the interpolated direction in lighting.
The source Phong shading name refers to normal interpolation, distinct from the Phong specular reflection model.
Smooth brightness does not change a hexagonal silhouette; normals alone do not move the surface or reshape holes.

scenes.title: 평평한 갑판과 굽은 난간의 경계
lines: Characters move on Big Walk red deck; observe the broad floor, curved rail and tilted control panels.
Smooth shading directions and geometric boundaries differ; distinguish intended smooth surfaces from hard joins.
Now accumulate all neighboring face directions and split sharing at the required boundaries.

scenes.title: 둥근 구멍과 평평한 벽을 함께 보기
lines: Walk between yellow structures in Big Walk, observing broad flat walls and circular opening boundaries.
Changing views reveal brightness and shadows; variation within a face differs from the opening outline.
A character passing through reveals thickness and passage space, distinct from smooth shading directions.
We cannot infer vertex counts or normal generation here; the question is why fixed coarse geometry can shade more smoothly.
Normals provide the answer. We next show the complete accumulation of neighboring face directions.
Flat walls and smooth curves need different directions; unconditional averaging can incorrectly shade sharp corners.
Revisit wall and opening boundaries and consider which directions should blend and which should remain separate.

scenes.title: 이웃 면의 법선을 끝까지 합산하기
lines: Generate simple averaged normals for a mesh without them, starting every vertex accumulator at zero.
Cross each triangle edges; reject or report nearly-zero degenerate faces before normalization.
Normalize a valid face normal and add it to each of the three indexed vertex accumulators.
One right, up and front direction sum to(1,1,1); dividing by square root three gives components about.577.
After processing every face, normalize each nonzero sum; dividing by face count first preserves the final direction.
Isolated vertices and canceling directions can produce zero sums; use explicit split, authored-normal or error policies.
This basic algorithm gives each face one vote; sharp boundaries and triangulation bias need separate treatment.

scenes.title: 모서리에서 정점을 복제하는 이유
lines: Three cube faces meet at a corner; sharing one shading normal blends their directions and brightness boundaries.
The cube geometry stays fixed but can shade like a rounded object; intentional hard edges must not blend directions.
Duplicate records at equal positions: a cube with eight locations can use six faces times four, or24 records.
Store the top normal in top-face records and side normals in side records, updating indices accordingly.
UV seams can require equal positions pointing to different image locations, also requiring separate records.
Opposing normals on two-sided leaves cancel to zero; split the sides or define two-sided orientation treatment explicitly.
Duplicating records need not open a physical gap; it separates attributes and logical references while tools can preserve geometric adjacency.

scenes.title: 삼각형 수가 많으면 그 방향이 이길까요?
lines: Suppose two top triangles and two side faces meet at a vertex; equal face votes give the top direction two votes.
Axis-aligned votes sum to(1,2,1), normalized to approximately(.408,.816,.408), biased upward.
Changing a quad diagonal changes which vertices touch two triangles, potentially altering averages without changing the surface.
Angle weighting uses the corner angle: splitting a quad corner ninety degrees preserves its total ninety.
Accumulate angle times direction and normalize; other policies such as area weighting approximate different intended surfaces.
Weighting does not fix intentionally sharp cubes; first separate hard edges, then average only intended smooth regions.

scenes.title: 평평한 면과 둥근 경계의 역할을 나누기
lines: Move to another opening in the yellow structure, observing broad planes and curved boundaries up close.
Viewing a character through the opening produces a clear silhouette boundary that smooth shading cannot remove.
Distinguish gradual surface directions from sharp joins without measuring this model vertex-record count.
Our cube example split directions at equal positions, whereas intended smooth interiors blend neighboring directions.
The choice aligns shading with shape, rather than universally minimizing records or averaging every join.
Now imagine stretching a shape horizontally: normal directions must change, but applying the position transform directly can fail.
Next we verify perpendicularity with explicitly defined tangent and normal values, without reverse-engineering brightness from pixels.

scenes.title: 정점 공유와 법선 만들기를 검산하기
lines: Four32-byte vertices and six2-byte indices total140 bytes; distinguish whole-mesh storage from a local shared-record calculation.
One index shares an entire record; equal positions with different normals or UVs require distinct records.
The basic algorithm initializes, computes valid face normals, accumulates at three vertices and normalizes last, with explicit zero/degenerate handling.
Split cube hard edges and choose a weighting policy on smooth regions; averaging directions does not round silhouettes.
Next we transform normals while preserving perpendicularity and calculate UV coordinates that map image patterns.
